gaps: Every breath-one unit assumed the two parties could count the new unit and were the only two parties. Sharpening Paternity test against a pollination contract, where the outcome nobody can count is priced per hive with a frame inspection, showed the unit settling not where value is but where both sides can count, and moving when a new counter arrives. This produced the changed question for breath two: what must be true of the thing sold for a unit to be pricable at all, and who hosts the meter.
accepted: Assay eats the item: per thing becomes per measured property of the thing, as milk is paid by butterfat and protein rather than the gallon, coal by heat content with penalties for sulfur, and cattle on a carcass grid, so the measurement burden moves to a grader both sides accept and the seller begins breeding, mining, and feeding toward the assay; not a finer price on the same unit, since the buyer now buys the property and the thing that carried it becomes invisible.

Cubed out: the priced unit migrates to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first, as a parcel carrier bills by cubic volume once its trucks fill before they weigh, and the shipping container turned per-ton handling into per-box lifts that never see the cargo; the buyer answers by packing to the unit, and what fights it is every good whose shape the unit punishes; not a unit chosen to measure value, but the seller's bottleneck given a price.

Rent on the peak: per unit consumed becomes per unit of capacity held ready, as a factory pays a demand charge on its highest kilowatt rather than its kilowatt-hours, a shipper leases a dedicated lane, and a cloud tenant reserves instances that sit idle in its name; the buyer now carries utilization risk and the seller is paid to be idle on the buyer's behalf, the peak becomes visible and the average invisible; not an option that may be oversold, since the reservation must hold at the very moment everyone wants it.

Sold your forecast of yourself: per use becomes per right to use, as a gym membership, a season pass, or a buffet, and the seller's margin is the gap between what the buyer expects to consume and what they do, pooled across buyers so the heavy user is carried by the absent one; the buyer's intention becomes visible and their consumption invisible, and what fights it is whoever consumes as much as they expected to; not a reservation, since nothing is held for anyone and the seller sells more rights than it could honor at once.

Thrust by the hour: per machine becomes per hour the machine works, with the seller keeping title and the maintenance, as an airline pays an engine maker per flight hour and a truck fleet pays a tyre maker per kilometre; the seller now carries reliability risk and so gets to design for repair, the meter moves onto the buyer's premises as telemetry, and the buyer's duty cycle becomes visible to the seller while the machine's price disappears; not a lease, since the buyer pays for work done rather than for time held.

Fence around done: per hour becomes per fixed scope, so the price stops measuring effort and starts measuring the completeness of a description, and whoever holds the pen on the description holds the margin, as construction change orders are where a fixed bid is really priced; the seller carries estimation risk, the buyer carries specification risk, effort becomes invisible, and what fights it is scope that grows and corners that get cut; not a coarser time unit, since a day rate still buys time.

Paternity test: per seat becomes per outcome, as software billed per resolved ticket, per hire, or per dollar collected, and an outcome has many parents, so the unit is pricable only when a rule of attribution both sides accept exists before the work; the seller now carries the buyer's competence risk, usage becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who can starve the counter; not a bonus on top of a seat price, since without the attribution rule there is no unit at all.

Paid for the nothing: per treatment becomes per event avoided, as pest control sold as a pest-free season or an energy contractor paid from the bill that never arrived, and a non-event cannot be counted, so the price is pinned to a baseline both sides must fix before the work: last year's count, the untreated strip, the neighbor's field; the fight moves entirely onto the baseline and the work itself becomes invisible; not outcome pricing with a minus sign, since attribution has nothing to attach to and only a control can stand in.

Head count over hand count: per visit or per repair becomes per head per period with the risk inside, as a clinic on capitation or an extended warranty, so the seller becomes an insurer and the unit is pricable only where heads can be pooled and cannot be chosen after pricing; the seller now wants to select the panel, the panel's risk profile becomes visible and the visit invisible, and which hazard appears depends on who holds the throttle on the event, neglect when the buyer does and stinting when the seller does; not a retainer, which buys availability rather than a person's risk.

Audit is the unit: per unit sold becomes per share of the buyer's take, as percentage rent in a mall, a royalty, a sharecropper's third, or a bookseller's right of return, so the seller must be able to see the buyer's till and the contract's real unit is the audit right; the seller now carries the buyer's market risk, the buyer's whole business becomes visible, and what fights it is a second till and every accounting that routes revenue around the counter; not a price set on the seller's own cost, which becomes invisible.

Hostage shelf: per copy becomes per continued access, as software, film, and music sold by subscription, so the buyer's past purchases become a stake forfeited on exit and the switching cost grows with tenure; the seller acquires the obligation to stay alive and keep serving, churn becomes visible and the marginal copy invisible, and what fights it is the buyer who wanted to own; not a lease of one thing, since what is held hostage is everything the buyer accumulated.

residue.item: Priced by the clock: per unit becomes per unit at this hour, as time-of-use power or surge fares.
residue.why: Folded into Rent on the peak: both price the buyer's position against the seller's peak, and spot versus advance commitment is a difference in when the buyer commits, not in the kind of thing bought.

residue.item: Door fee: per item becomes per right to buy at cost, as a warehouse-club membership.
residue.why: Rejected: it adds a unit beside the old one rather than changing its kind, since the member still pays per item; what the added unit is, a sold right to use, is already Sold your forecast of yourself.

residue.item: Shelf becomes a stage: per unit shipped becomes per unit sold through, as consignment and the bookseller's right of return.
residue.why: Merged into Audit is the unit as its unit-level case: the retailer's till becomes the unit either way, and the seller's obligation is the same right to see it.

residue.item: Pooled the dice: per repair becomes per premium, as an extended warranty, kept apart from capitation.
residue.why: Merged into Head count over hand count: poolability and post-pricing selection are the same mechanism in both; the real difference, who holds the throttle on the event, is carried in that item's discriminator rather than earning a second item.

residue.item: Take or pay: per unit with a paid-for floor, as a pipeline contract.
residue.why: Merged into Rent on the peak as its hybrid form: the floor is a reservation and the units above it are per use, two of the map's units in one contract rather than a third kind.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real contract usually carries several of these units at once (a two-part tariff is two of them), and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

The seriation is an itinerary of how far the priced unit has traveled from the thing handed over, not a ranking of sophistication, margin, or historical order; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (milk component pricing, engine flight-hour contracts, pollination rentals, chantries, per-mile insurance, streaming pools) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the specific contracts or their histories.

Dead counter's meter-decay mechanism and Nearest countable's claim that the unit moves toward the newest meter are conjectures held with visible modality; the near probe is built to test the first, and neither is asserted as established.
Changes of price on an unchanged unit (levels, tiers, indexing, surge) and changes of the money (scrip, cigarettes) are outside; only a change in the kind of thing the buyer is buying is in.

gaps: The changed question yielded units counted only by the seller (Meter in the seller's house), by a fourth party (Reader becomes the ton), by nobody, so that the losers' unbilled attempts are the price (Losers pay the winner), a general law of where units settle (Nearest countable), the one-way road that law implies (Dead counter), a seller whose price is a quotient (Quotient, not price), and a unit that is the seller's survival (Bought the forever). The territory pointer stands and the slug is kept, but the of-sentence now ends on what must be true of the thing sold for the unit to be pricable at all. The pointer's per-transaction-becomes-per-relationship dissolved into three existing items and left a seed; the invented world in which only the seller may count dissolved into the observed per-token case.
accepted: Meter in the seller's house: the unit becomes a quantity only the seller can count, as per-seat software becomes per-token inference and the buyer pays a bill they cannot audit for a tokenizer they cannot see; the measurement burden leaves the buyer and returns as trust, the cost of verbosity becomes visible while value becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who cannot forecast next month's invoice; not a hidden price, since the rate is published, but a hidden count.

Nearest countable: a unit settles on the closest thing both parties can count and moves the day a new counter arrives, as almond growers rent bees per hive with a frame inspection because nobody can count pollinations, and car insurance moved from per year toward per mile once an odometer plug could be mailed to the buyer; not a proxy chosen for accuracy, since the unit moves toward the newest meter rather than the truest measure (conjectural as a general law, observed in the two cases).

Dead counter: a unit change is reversible only while the old unit's meter is still kept, and nobody is paid to keep a meter no unit bills on, so the road back closes behind the move, as a shop that went from hourly to fixed bid and stopped its timesheets can return to hourly only by bidding blind for a season; not lock-in by contract but by the decay of a measurement, a conjectured mechanism the near probe is built to test.

Losers pay the winner: per hour of search becomes per first solution, as a prize, a bounty, or a design competition, so the unit is one success and its price is paid mostly by sellers who never meet the buyer, in failed attempts nobody bills; the buyer carries no risk and the seller population carries all of it, and what becomes invisible is the whole cost of the search; not outcome pricing between two parties, since the buyer buys from a crowd and the crowd's losses are the price.

Quotient, not price: when the buyer's per-copy payment becomes one flat stream and the sellers stay many, the seller's unit becomes a share of a pool, as a streaming payout per play is the month's pot divided by the month's plays; the seller's price ceases to be a number anyone can set, and what becomes invisible is any way for one seller to charge more; not a low price but the absence of one, a residual that looks like a rate.

Reader becomes the ton: per copy becomes per thousand of the reader's attention sold to someone else, as a newspaper's price falls to zero and its unit becomes the impression, so the payer and the unit change places and neither buyer nor seller can count what is sold; a fourth party must host the meter, the ratings panel or the tracker, and what fights it is the reader who blocks the counter; not a discount to the reader, since the reader has stopped being the buyer.

Bought the forever: per event becomes per perpetuity, as a medieval donor stopped paying per mass and endowed a chantry to say them without end, so the unit is the seller's continued existence and the thing is pricable only if the seller is an institution that can outlive the buyer; the hostage flips sides, since the endowment holds the monastery to its masses, and what fights it is dissolution rather than churn; not a long subscription, since nothing is renewed and nobody can stop paying.

residue.item: Coarser clock: per hour becomes per day or per sprint.
residue.why: Rejected as the boundary nonmember: the buyer still buys time and nobody's burden or risk moves; a change of grain on the same unit is a change of price.

residue.item: Meter makes the reversal: a pooled unit returns to per use when a cheap witness of use appears, as per-mile insurance with an odometer plug.
residue.why: Folded into Nearest countable as its dynamic case, since the arrival of a meter moving the unit is that item's law in motion; Dead counter keeps the opposite direction, where the meter's death blocks the way back.

residue.item: Third of the crop: per acre of rent becomes per share of the harvest.
residue.why: Merged into Audit is the unit as its oldest case; sharecropping obliges the same sight of the tenant's take, with the field standing in for the till.

residue.item: Box hides the cargo: per ton handled becomes per container lifted, and the contents vanish from the price.
residue.why: Merged into Cubed out: the container is the seller's handling constraint given a price, the same migration as dimensional weight; kept as that item's second case so the contents' invisibility survives.

residue.item: Cigarette standard: a prison economy prices favors in packs of cigarettes or ramen.
residue.why: Rejected: a change of the money, not of the unit priced; the pack still buys a per-favor unit, and the map's type is the unit, not the currency.

residue.item: Per transaction becomes per relationship, from the territory pointer.
residue.why: Dissolved rather than admitted: under pressure it split three ways, into an assigned person-period with risk (Head count over hand count), a paid availability (Rent on the peak), and tenure that holds the buyer's stake (Hostage shelf); a relationship priced as such may be the absence of a unit rather than one, and that is the open seed.

residue.item: An invented world in which only the seller may count.
residue.why: Dissolved into an observed arrangement: per-token inference billed on a tokenizer the buyer cannot see, which became Meter in the seller's house without needing the invented premise.

neighbors.left: Rent on the peak: per unit consumed becomes per unit of capacity held ready, as a factory pays a demand charge on its highest kilowatt rather than its kilowatt-hours, a shipper leases a dedicated lane, and a cloud tenant reserves instances that sit idle in its name; the buyer now carries utilization risk and the seller is paid to be idle on the buyer's behalf, the peak becomes visible and the average invisible; not an option that may be oversold, since the reservation must hold at the very moment everyone wants it.
neighbors.right: Sold your forecast of yourself: per use becomes per right to use, as a gym membership, a season pass, or a buffet, and the seller's margin is the gap between what the buyer expects to consume and what they do, pooled across buyers so the heavy user is carried by the absent one; the buyer's intention becomes visible and their consumption invisible, and what fights it is whoever consumes as much as they expected to; not a reservation, since nothing is held for anyone and the seller sells more rights than it could honor at once.
neighbors.separating_case: One coworking floor sold two ways. A dedicated desk is Rent on the peak: held empty in the tenant's name, the seller paid to keep it idle, and the reservation good on the day everyone shows up. A hot-desk membership on the same floor is Sold your forecast of yourself: more memberships than desks, the margin in the members who stay home, and on the day everyone shows up the unit fails. Same desk, same price, different unit: one is a promise that must hold at the peak, the other a bet that the peak never comes.

checks.boundary_case: Per hour becoming per day, or per unit becoming a volume tier, is out: the buyer still buys time or units, and nobody's measurement burden or risk moves, so a coarser or curved price on the same unit is a change of price, not of kind. Fence around done is in on exactly that contrast, since a fixed bid stops buying time at all.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence hides as adjacency: Paternity test → Paid for the nothing splits outcome pricing on the sign of the event, and the two branches need different instruments, an attribution rule for what occurred and a baseline for what did not. It shows an incompatibility between two itinerary neighbors, Sold your forecast of yourself and Thrust by the hour: both price the buyer's use of something the seller keeps, but the option unit lives on the buyer not seeing their utilization and the metered unit exists to show it, so one contract cannot carry both on the same unit. It shows a passage between levels at Hostage shelf → Quotient, not price, where a change in the buyer's unit forces a change in the seller's unit and the seller's price disappears, and a second passage at Reader becomes the ton → Meter in the seller's house, where the meter leaves both parties' houses for a fourth party's. And it shows a broken loop at Nearest countable → Dead counter: the line reads as if a unit could walk back along the itinerary, and the edge says the ford is one-way because the meter behind it dies.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each admitted item names a different thing the new unit obliges and a different party who ends up counting or carrying; the strange members (a price that is a quotient, a unit that is the seller's survival, a price paid by losers who never meet the buyer, a reader who becomes the ton) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into pricing advice.

next_crossfield_opening: A unit is a witness architecture for value: connect Nearest countable and Meter in the seller's house with witness-architectures' Common meter and Ledger that makes the debt, and question-metamorphoses' Debt in the units; ask whether a unit whose meter only one party hosts is a witness to a quantity or a ledger that makes the debt, and whether Quotient, not price is the case where the unit constitutes the price outright.

gaps: The two most generative items, Nearest countable and Dead counter, were laws about how units move rather than transformations of the declared type, and Nearest countable's 'both parties can count' was contradicted by the map's own one-sided meters (tokens, impressions, plays); the real law is the nearest counter both sides will accept, whoever hosts it. Dead counter's timesheet case showed a different mechanism than claimed: the new unit is priced from the old meter's records and goes blind when it dies. Four of seven edge labels asserted a must or cannot against standing counterexamples (telecom allowance plans, fixed per-play platform rates, a search company counting its own clicks, per-year insurance reopening at will), so the incompatibility and the one-way ford survive only as conditionals.
accepted: Nearest countable: an outcome nobody can count retreats to the nearest thing a counter both sides accept can inspect, and advances again the day a new counter arrives, as almond growers pay per hive with a frame inspection because pollination cannot be counted, and car insurance moved from per year toward per mile once an odometer plug could be mailed to the buyer; the counter need not be either party, since tokens, impressions, and plays are counted by one side or a fourth and the other side merely accepts; not a proxy chosen for accuracy, since the unit moves toward the newest accepted meter rather than the truest measure (conjectural as a general law, observed in the two cases).

Dead counter: per hour becomes per fixed bid, and the new unit is priced from the old one's records for exactly as long as they are kept, since nobody is paid to keep a meter no unit bills on; a shop that dropped its timesheets when it went to fixed bids is estimating blind within a season, and cannot price a return to hourly estimates either, so the road back closes only behind a move that abandoned a meter, while per-year insurance, which needed no odometer, reopens at will; not lock-in by contract but by the decay of a measurement, a conjectured mechanism the near probe is built to test.

Hostage shelf: per copy becomes per continued access, as software holding the buyer's files and music holding the buyer's playlists sold by subscription, so the buyer's past purchases become a stake forfeited on exit and the switching cost grows with tenure; the seller acquires the obligation to stay alive and keep serving, churn becomes visible and the marginal copy invisible, and what fights it is the buyer who wanted to own; not a lease of one thing, and not film by subscription, where nothing accumulates and the margin is only the light viewer's absence, since what is held hostage is everything the buyer accumulated.

Meter in the seller's house: the unit becomes a quantity only the seller can count, as per-seat software becomes per-token inference and the buyer pays a bill they cannot audit for reasoning tokens they are billed for and never receive; the measurement burden leaves the buyer and returns as trust, the cost of verbosity becomes visible while value becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who cannot forecast next month's invoice; not a hidden price, since the rate is published, but a hidden count.

Cubed out: the priced unit tends to migrate to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first, as a parcel carrier bills by cubic volume once its trucks fill before they weigh, and the shipping container turned per-ton handling into per-box lifts that never see the cargo; the buyer answers by packing to the unit, and what fights it is every good whose shape the unit punishes, and the migration only completes where the constraint is something the buyer can measure too, a cube but not a queue; not a unit chosen to measure value, but the seller's bottleneck given a price (a tendency observed in freight, not asserted as a law).
limits: Dead counter's meter-decay mechanism, Nearest countable's claim that the unit moves toward the newest accepted meter, and Cubed out's migration toward the seller's binding constraint are conjectures held with visible modality; the near probe is built to test the first, none is asserted as established, and the map has no rule for which of the last two wins when they disagree.
seed: The map built a grammar of who hosts the meter: a grader both sides accept (Assay), the seller alone (tokens), a fourth party (the ratings panel), and nobody (the losers' unbilled attempts). It left out the buyer alone, after the fact: tipping, pay-what-you-want, the honor bar, where the count exists but the price of the service component is set by the counted party's customer after consumption. That is the mirror of Meter in the seller's house, a meter in the buyer's house, and it would test whether the map's laws of unit motion run symmetrically: does a unit also settle on the nearest counter the seller will accept, and does a buyer-hosted meter die the same way? Behind it sits the second seed: the map now carries two attractors, the seller's binding constraint (Cubed out) and the nearest accepted counter (Nearest countable), and has no rule for which wins when they disagree.
